primitives.name: Pregame Data Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Model boundary The independent model receives only facts and provenance captured before first pitch.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes all features are observable and recorded prior to game start.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime where any post-first-pitch data causes the observation to be excluded.

layer2.mapping: Enforces a temporal causality constraint similar to a lagged feature set in time-series analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Anti-collinearity condition is the absence of correlation between pregame features and post-first-pitch outcomes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitive establishes a formal separation between model development and deployment. By shipping a fail-closed API, it ensures that an unfitted model cannot inadvertently influence production decisions. This is critical because near-zero resolution in the current confidence path introduces systematic bias, which could be masked by retuning the consensus scorer. Instead, we create a dedicated sandbox where the new model's probability structure P(Target|BaseballFacts) can be independently verified against historical outcomes without leaking post-first-pitch information. The null probability serves as a sentinel value, signaling when the model is not yet calibrated. This approach mitigates the risk of overfitting to consensus signals and provides a transparent pathway to model promotion once rigorous validation metrics are met.
